gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a price for any station. At US maker-store prices on 2026-11-13, the BLUETTI Elite 300 ($1,199, 3,014.4 Wh, $0.40/Wh) is the cheapest in-stock station big enough for a 24-hour heated 75-gallon tank (about 2.45 kWh at 20% heater duty). Every 2 kWh unit ($879–$1,049) ends up about 700 Wh short. The next in-stock unit of 3 kWh or more, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra, costs $100 more, and the ALLPOWERS R4000 is sold out.
standout_why: I compared planetfish.org (8 picks), colovma.com (8 picks), ouraquariumlife.com (5 battery air pumps) and the cited reefs.com Elite 100 V2 test. None of them states a single dollar price: planetfish and colovma only have 'Check Price' links, ouraquariumlife only has budget tiers, and reefs.com gives no price. None ranks stations by price against a 24-hour heated-tank energy budget. planetfish's largest pick, the Anker SOLIX S2000 (2,010 Wh), ran a 95 W tank for 19 h 22 min, so it falls short of 24 h by its own numbers. Petco covers no products. The only price ChatGPT showed for the Elite 300 ($1,199) came from our own page, flagged 'not independently verified'. The R4000 being sold out, the DELTA 3 Ultra price comparison and the DELTA 3 Max at $879 appear nowhere in the results.
decides: This confirms the Elite 300 as the pick, and on price rather than capacity alone. It is the cheapest in-stock unit that clears about 2.45 kWh usable, and it costs less than the 2,048 Wh DELTA 2 Max plus a second battery. It argues against ChatGPT's other two answers, which led with 2,048 Wh units (DELTA 2 Max $1,049 at Home Depot, DELTA 3 Max $879 at Best Buy). At 85% usable (about 1,740 Wh), those run a 100 W average load for about 17 h. Spending $1,199 instead of $879 buys roughly 820 more usable Wh, which is the gap between dark at hour 17 and making it to 24. Our page's ALLPOWERS R4000 row needs a 'sold out on iallpowers.com' flag, and the DELTA 3 Ultra should be added as the same-size alternative that costs $100 more.

findings.label: US maker-store price
findings.note: Shopify store data via storecheck. $1,199 / 3,014.4 Wh = $0.398/Wh. At 85% usable that is about 2,562 Wh, which clears ChatGPT's own 2,448 Wh budget (300 W heater at 20% duty, 23 W filter, 4 W air pump, 15 W overhead) by about 114 Wh. That margin is thin, and it is gone at 30% duty (3.2 kWh). It is the cheapest in-stock unit I found that clears the 20%-duty budget.
